cues.en: Welcome to this episode of the Common Sense Skeptic. This episode is going to be dedicated to Musk's Internet constellation called Starlink,
cues.zh: 欢迎收看本期《常识怀疑论者》。本期节目将专门讨论马斯克的互联网星座计划——Starlink，

cues.en: which we touched on in our colonizing Mars series. We touched on it because this is the service where Musk wrote the outline for a free and independent Mars into one of the sections of the service agreement.
cues.zh: 我们在火星殖民系列中曾提到过它。之所以提到，是因为这项服务的服务协议中有一节，马斯克在其中写下了自由独立火星的构想。

cues.en: We are going to take this topic on from a couple of different angles. The economic model, the benefits over competitors, and the hazards that this system presents if it is allowed to continue forward.
cues.zh: 我们将从几个不同角度探讨这个话题：经济模式、相对竞争对手的优势，以及如果允许这一系统继续推进将会带来的危害。

cues.en: Musk has convinced his followers that Starlink will provide the economic boon that SpaceX needs to finance all of their future space endeavors.
cues.zh: Musk 让他的追随者相信，Starlink 将带来经济收益，为 SpaceX 未来所有的太空计划提供资金。

cues.en: Several articles believe that this is a $30,000,000,000
cues.zh: 有几篇文章认为，到 2025 年，这会成为一家价值 300 亿美元的

cues.en: cash cow for the company by the year 2025,
cues.zh: 现金牛，

cues.en: so just four years from now. We are going to demonstrate that they are kidding themselves if they think this is going to happen, and we're going to start within the historical precedent.
cues.zh: 也就是仅仅四年之后。我们将证明，如果他们以为这会发生，那就是在自欺欺人。我们先从历史先例说起。

cues.en: Apparently,
cues.zh: 显然，

cues.en: the core of his followers suffer from a lack of long term memory because they've been played like this before. It wasn't that long ago that they believed Musk when he was selling them leases and PPAs for solar panel systems through SolarCity,
cues.zh: 他的核心信徒们似乎记性不太好，毕竟以前就被这么忽悠过。就在不久前，Musk 通过 SolarCity 向他们推销太阳能板系统的租赁和购电协议（PPA）时，他们也是深信不疑，

cues.en: while claiming to be revolutionizing
cues.zh: 当时他还宣称要颠覆

cues.en: the entire solar industry.
cues.zh: 整个太阳能行业。

cues.en: To recap that model, subscribers to SolarCity would get a free installation and solar array with no upfront cost by signing a long term contract.
cues.zh: 回顾一下那种模式，SolarCity 的订购用户只要签一份长期合同，就能免费安装太阳能电池阵列，完全没有前期费用。

cues.en: The company fronted the equipment and the installation cost, and they collected lease payments on those systems.
cues.zh: 公司先垫付了设备和安装费用，然后通过收取这些系统的租赁费来回收。

cues.en: Another option was to allow SolarCity to install a system on your house for free, and then they would charge you for the power by the kilowatt hour that you used like any other utility.
cues.zh: 另一种选择是让SolarCity免费在你家安装系统，然后按你使用的千瓦时收费，就像其他公用事业一样。

cues.en: This was called a PPA,
cues.zh: 这被称为PPA，

cues.en: which was short for power purchase agreement.
cues.zh: 是电力购买协议的缩写。

cues.en: Both of these scenarios required SolarCity to cop up the initial equipment investment, which they financed by selling bonds, which were supposed to be secured by the future customer payments against these systems.
cues.zh: 这两种情况都需要SolarCity先掏钱投入初始设备，他们通过发行债券来融资，而这些债券本应由这些系统未来的客户付款来担保。

cues.en: Where the SolarCity model failed was that the installation and the equipment were costing more than the company could ever hope to recover through the subscription fees. And the more people that signed up for the service, the more bonds Musk had to sell to cover the new installs.
cues.zh: SolarCity 模式的问题在于，安装和设备的成本高得离谱，公司根本不可能靠订阅费收回成本。订阅的人越多，Musk 就越得卖债券，才能支付新增安装的费用。

cues.en: As it turns out, a lot of those bonds were purchased through his other companies using government money that was earmarked for other purposes.
cues.zh: 结果发现，很多债券是通过他的其他公司买下的，用的还是原本划拨给其他用途的政府资金。

cues.en: In the case of SpaceX,
cues.zh: 就 SpaceX 而言，

cues.en: Musk used money he received from NASA to develop Crew Dragon. We covered this in detail in our two part episode on Solar City, what Musk sold Tesla.
cues.zh: Musk 用了从 NASA 拿到的资金来研发 Crew Dragon。我们在关于 SolarCity 的上下两期节目中详细讲过这点，也就是 Musk 卖给 Tesla 的那家公司。

cues.en: By the time Musk bailed himself out using Tesla shareholders money, Solar City was $3,000,000,000
cues.zh: 等到 Musk 用 Tesla 股东的钱给自己解围时，SolarCity 已经背负了 30 亿美元

cues.en: in debt because this model had failed miserably.
cues.zh: 的债务，因为这种模式彻底失败了。

cues.en: This whole situation was so bad that there is presently a conflict of interest class action moving forward next month in Delaware, and we will be covering that as closely as we can. All other plaintiffs on that case have already pleaded out and paid fines because they could not defend their actions in allowing Tesla to buy SolarCity.
cues.zh: 整个情况极其恶劣，以至于下个月在特拉华州将有一场利益冲突集体诉讼开庭，我们也会尽可能跟进报道。该案中的所有其他被告都已经认罪并缴纳了罚款，因为他们根本无法为自己允许 Tesla 收购 SolarCity 的行为辩护。

cues.en: Now here we are with Star Link, and Musk is planning on doing the exact same thing. And the result will wind up being identical because that is pretty much unavoidable.
cues.zh: 现在我们有了星链，而马斯克正打算做一模一样的事。结果也会完全相同，因为这几乎不可避免。

cues.en: First off, what is StarLink? Starlink is an Internet receiving and transmitting dish about the size of a large pizza, and the package they sell includes the accompanying mount with the router and the cables that they require.
cues.zh: 首先，星链是什么？星链是一个互联网收发天线，大小和一个大披萨差不多，他们出售的套装还包括配套支架、路由器以及所需的线缆。

cues.en: Customers order the kit, arrange for the installation on their own dime, or they they do it themselves.
cues.zh: 客户订购这套设备，自费安排安装，或者自己动手装。

cues.en: No service personnel apparently are assigned that can do this for you. From the looks of it, most people are just putting it on the ground.
cues.zh: 显然，没有专门的维修人员能帮你处理这件事。从目前的情况看，大多数人只是把它放在地上。

cues.en: The dish you're buying is a sealed unit that not even experienced electronics technicians can take apart without completely destroying it.
cues.zh: 你买的这件餐具是密封的一体式产品，就连经验丰富的电子维修技师也无法在不彻底毁掉它的情况下拆开。

cues.en: This video on YouTube dubbed by Ken Kider shows the destruction required to access the hardware to see what makes it tick or to make any repairs.
cues.zh: 这段由 Ken Kider 配音的 YouTube 视频展示了，要接触内部硬件、弄清它的工作原理或进行维修，必须把它破坏到什么程度。

cues.en: And the dish, for whatever reason, has the cable leads attached directly to the dish instead of plugging in like a DAC or HDMI cable.
cues.zh: 不知为何，天线上的线缆引线是直接连在盘体上的，而不是像 DAC 或 HDMI 线那样可以插拔。

cues.en: So when the cable needs replacing,
cues.zh: 所以一旦需要更换线缆，

cues.en: it is possible you'll have to buy a whole new dish. Same thing if anything goes wrong with it. Toss the old one away and order a new one. And their very limited warranty runs out after one year, so keeping the thing safe and sound and out of the dirt might be a better idea than keeping it somewhere where your dog can pee on it. The interesting part about this array is that Starlink sells these directly to the customer for $500.
cues.zh: 你可能就得买个全新的天线。出任何故障也一样，只能把旧的扔掉再买个新的。而且他们极为有限的保修期只有一年，因此把它妥善保管、远离泥土，绝对比放在容易被狗尿到的地方更明智。关于这个天线阵列，有意思的是 Starlink 直接向客户以 500 美元的价格出售。

cues.en: According to teardown experts in the field, most likely these units cost the company about $2,000 to manufacture
cues.zh: 据该领域的拆解专家称，这些设备的生产成本很可能在每台2000美元左右

cues.en: and that manufacturing is outsourced, not done in house. The numbers you can find in articles online range from about $1,500
cues.zh: 而且生产是外包的，并非自己生产。网上文章里给出的数字大约从1500美元

cues.en: to over 3,000
cues.zh: 到3000多美元不等

cues.en: per dish. So we're going to use the $2,000 figure to be middle of the road and conservative.
cues.zh: 每台。所以我们取2000美元这个数字，属于中间偏保守的估计。

cues.en: So if it cost the company $2,000
cues.zh: 所以，如果公司造这台设备花了2000美元

cues.en: to build the unit and they sell it for $500,
cues.zh: 却只卖500美元，

cues.en: well, means that Starlink is losing about $1,500
cues.zh: 那就意味着Starlink每卖出一台设备大约亏损1500美元

cues.en: per dish that they've put out, and they can only recover that cost through the $100 a month subscription fee.
cues.zh: 而他们只能通过每月100美元的订阅费来收回这部分成本。

cues.en: Since the company claims to have 500,000
cues.zh: 既然这家公司声称目前有 50 万

cues.en: customers on a waiting list at this point in time, that suggests the company will have to carry $750,000,000
cues.zh: 名客户在等候名单上，这意味着光是发出这些套件，公司就得承担 7.5 亿美元

cues.en: in equipment cost just to send out those kits.
cues.zh: 的设备成本。

cues.en: But that is just the leading edge of the money pit where Starlink is concerned.
cues.zh: 但这只是 Starlink 这座吞金坑的冰山一角。

cues.en: That dish, affectionately referred to as Dishy McFlat face, is useless without a satellite to bounce signals off of. Musk has declared his intention is to launch 42,000
cues.zh: 这款被亲切地称为 Dishy McFlatface 的天线，没有卫星转发信号就毫无用处。马斯克宣称，他打算将 42,000

cues.en: satellites into orbit as a constellation to serve his customers.
cues.zh: 颗卫星送入轨道，组成星座，为客户提供服务。

cues.en: This is something we're going to revisit later, but for right now, we'll just take him at his word.
cues.zh: 这个我们稍后再回过头来看，但眼下，我们就先姑且信他的话。

cues.en: For the foreseeable future, Starship is nowhere near ready to deliver such payloads to orbit. And while we're showing this frame, let's just acknowledge that this has to be the dumbest configuration for a deployment bay ever.
cues.zh: 在可预见的未来，Starship 根本还没准备好把这类载荷送入轨道。既然画面正好停在这儿，我们不得不承认，这绝对是有史以来最蠢的载荷舱设计。

cues.en: Single hinge point on around the surface, no clear exit for your payload, no robotic arm, those satellites are going to bounce off of everything, and probably smack that front door open permanently.
cues.zh: 在弧形表面上就单铰链连接，载荷没有明确的弹出通道，没有机械臂，那些卫星肯定会到处乱撞，八成还会把舱门直接彻底撞飞。

cues.en: No Starlink devices have been delivered to orbit using a Falcon Heavy. Wonder why that is since it's apparently a functional system with a far greater payload capacity.
cues.zh: 目前还没有任何星链设备通过猎鹰重型火箭送入轨道。想知道为什么吗，毕竟它显然是一个功能正常的系统，有效载荷能力还大得多。

cues.en: Yet to date, the only things it's launched into space were the Roadster that Musk stole from Martin Eberhardt in 2018,
cues.zh: 但迄今为止，它送入太空的东西只有马斯克2018年从Martin Eberhardt那里夺来的Roadster，

cues.en: the AeroSat six a mission in April 2019,
cues.zh: 2019年4月的AeroSat六号任务，

cues.en: and the DOD mission the same June.
cues.zh: 以及同年6月的国防部任务。

cues.en: Dragon heavy hasn't flown for over two years, leaving only Falcon nines to make these orbital insertions carrying 60 of these satellites at a time, and they want to launch 42,000
cues.zh: 猎鹰重型已经两年多没飞了，只剩下猎鹰九号来执行这些轨道插入任务，每次携带60颗这类卫星，而他们想发射42000

cues.en: satellites,
cues.zh: 颗卫星，

cues.en: meaning they will need to launch 700
cues.zh: 这意味着他们需要发射700

cues.en: Falcon nines to get the job done.
cues.zh: 次猎鹰九号才能完成这项工作。

cues.en: Cost of a Falcon nine launch as charged to the US government who paid them to develop the technology
cues.zh: 向美国政府收取的 Falcon 9 发射费用，而政府此前还资助他们研发了这项技术
是5000万美元

cues.en: for a reused booster or $62,000,000
cues.zh: 如果是重复使用的助推器，或者花费 6200 万美元

cues.en: if they're using a new one.
cues.zh: 如果他们用的是个新的。

cues.en: Again, we'll split the difference at $55,000,000
cues.zh: 再折中一下，定在 5500 万美元。

cues.en: per launch and assume that covers every aspect of launching the vehicle, including pad lease fees, staff paychecks, and every other associated cost with a launch.
cues.zh: 每次发射的成本假设涵盖了运载器发射的所有方面，包括发射台租赁费、员工工资，以及发射相关的其他所有成本。

cues.en: 700 launches later, that simple math totals $38,500,000,000
cues.zh: 700次发射之后，按这简单的算术总计就是385亿美元

cues.en: just for the launch vehicles.
cues.zh: 仅就运载火箭而言。

cues.en: The satellites have a reported aspirational cost of $250,000
cues.zh: 据报道，这些卫星的理想目标成本是 25 万美元

cues.en: per unit. Again, that's an aspirational target for the manufacturing cost, not the cost to date, which has been reported to be as high as $500,000
cues.zh: 每颗。再说一次，这只是制造成本的理想目标，并非目前的实际成本，据报道目前单颗成本高达 50 万美元。

cues.en: per unit. To stay on the conservative side, we'll once again use their dream number.
cues.zh: 保守起见，我们还是采用他们这个最理想的数字。

cues.en: The cost of 42,000 of those carries a price tag of $10,500,000,000.
cues.zh: 造 42,000 颗卫星的造价高达 105 亿美元。

cues.en: Current failure rate of the Starlink constellation in orbit is three percent, and most of them are less than a year old.
cues.zh: 目前在轨的 Starlink 星座故障率是 3%，而且其中大多数发射还不到一年。

cues.en: To keep the eventual constellation full, that will require launching an additional 1,260
cues.zh: 为保持最终星座完整，每年需要额外发射1，260

cues.en: satellites per year to keep up performance, requiring another $2,155,000,000
cues.zh: 颗卫星以维持性能，这又需要另外2，155，000，000

cues.en: dollar launches.
cues.zh: 美元的发射费用。

cues.en: Additional cost to replace the damaged units will total $1,155,000,000
cues.zh: 替换受损单元的额外成本总计将达1，155，000，000

cues.en: for the launches and $315,000,000
cues.zh: 美元用于发射，以及315，000，000

cues.en: for the satellites. So call that $1,500,000,000
cues.zh: 美元用于卫星。所以算下来每年是1，500，000，000

cues.en: annually
cues.zh: 美元

cues.en: just for upkeep.
cues.zh: 仅用于维护。

cues.en: Then there's the staff at SpaceX to consider. The company claims to have 10,000 workers under its umbrella, and they expect Starlink to become a major income generator for their company. We discovered that starting wage for a Starlink junior production position is a fairly weak 32,000 per year per employee salary cost.
cues.zh: 然后还要考虑SpaceX的员工。该公司声称旗下有10，000名员工，他们期望Starlink成为公司的主要收入来源。我们发现，Starlink初级生产岗位的起薪相当低，每名员工每年的薪资成本为32，000美元。

cues.en: But the cost of employee to the company including deductions, benefits, insurances, etcetera, increases that cost by up to 40%.
cues.zh: 但员工给公司带来的成本，包括扣款、福利、保险等，最高会增加 40%。

cues.en: So the entry positions will actually cost the company about $45,675
cues.zh: 所以初级岗位的实际用人成本大约是 45,675 美元

cues.en: per head if all they're making is entry level wages, which comes to about $500,000,000
cues.zh: 按人头算，如果他们只拿入门级工资，那大约是5亿美元。

cues.en: per year in salaries to service only 500,000
cues.zh: 每年薪资支出就能服务 50 万人

cues.en: subscribers.
cues.zh: 订阅者。

cues.en: Combine that in with the annual failure rate, and that's $2,000,000,000
cues.zh: 把年故障率也算进去，就是20亿美元

cues.en: per year.
cues.zh: 每年。

cues.en: That's not counting any lease spaces, utilities, licensing fees, or the network of ground stations that this system requires in order to actually access the World Wide Web. At $100 per month, the company will need 1,750,000
cues.zh: 这还没算上场地租赁、水电费、牌照许可费，以及接入互联网所需的地面站网络成本。按每月 100 美元计算，该公司需要 175 万

cues.en: subscribers
cues.zh: 名订阅读者

cues.en: just to cover the extra launches and salaries without biting into the initial cost of setup at all.
cues.zh: 才能勉强覆盖额外发射和员工薪水，这还完全没算初期的搭建成本。

cues.en: And remember, we use the conservative estimates on all these numbers. If the satellite costs are $500,000
cues.zh: 别忘了，这些数字我们用的都还是保守估计。如果单颗卫星的成本达到 50 万美元，

cues.en: per and the launches run $62,000,000
cues.zh: 单次发射费用高达 6200 万美元，

cues.en: per launch, these numbers jump significantly
cues.zh: 那么仅部署完整个卫星星座，

cues.en: just to get the constellation in place.
cues.zh: 成本数字就会大幅飙升。

cues.en: But here's one more thing to throw into the mix. According to Gwen Shotwell, president at SpaceX, the entire array will have to be replaced every five years, a five year lifespan on the satellite modules.
cues.zh: 但这还有一点要考虑。据SpaceX总裁Gwen Shotwell所说，整个阵列每五年就得更换一次，卫星模块的使用寿命只有五年。

cues.en: So in five years, we'll have 42,000
cues.zh: 所以五年后，会有42000

cues.en: pieces of space junk floating around in orbit being replaced by another 42,000
cues.zh: 块太空垃圾在轨道上漂浮，然后每五年再被另外42000块替换掉。

cues.en: every five years. The entire premise is asinine.
cues.zh: 整个设想荒谬至极。

cues.en: And then the company expects to make $30,000,000,000
cues.zh: 然后公司还指望在此基础上每年赚300亿美元？

cues.en: per year on top of this?
cues.zh: 每年？

cues.en: At $100 per month subscription fees, that will require another 2,500,000
cues.zh: 按每月 100 美元的订阅费计算，还需要再增加 2,500,000 名

cues.en: subscribers,
cues.zh: 订阅用户，

cues.en: which will need another 2,500,000
cues.zh: 这又需要再增加 2,500,000 台

cues.en: terminals, which will cost the company another $37,500,000,000
cues.zh: 终端设备，公司还要为此承担 37,500,000,000 美元的设备成本。

cues.en: in equipment cost, which means they will need more customers that will cost them more money, and the cycle will never end.
cues.zh: 这意味着他们需要更多客户，而获取这些客户又要花更多钱，这个循环永远不会结束。

cues.en: The second part of this is going to compare the service customers would receive against other services currently offering Internet in North America.
cues.zh: 接下来，我们会把客户能获得的服务与目前北美其他互联网服务进行比较。

cues.en: Of course, we're going to deal specifically with the satellite service providers since Starlink specs can't and will never match specs on a typical telecom provider Internet service.
cues.zh: 当然，我们这次专门讨论卫星服务提供商，因为 Starlink 的规格不可能、也永远无法与传统电信运营商的有线宽带相比。

cues.en: In case anyone is unaware,
cues.zh: 以防有人还不了解，

cues.en: generally speaking, satellites have little to nothing to do with providing normal Internet service through your local cable or telecom provider.
cues.zh: 一般来说，大家平时用的有线或电信宽带，基本完全用不到卫星。

cues.zh: 毫无疑问，Shotwell 在这场辩论中完全摸不着头脑。在 Gwynne Shotwell 和亿万富翁投资者 Ron Baron 的一次现场访谈中，他向她抛出了这个问题：当你们在轨道上有成千上万颗卫星时，怎么能确保不会撞上其他卫星呢？

cues.en: Her response,
cues.zh: 而她的回答是：

cues.en: think about 30,000 people on Earth spread out fairly evenly. You could spend your whole life and never see another person.
cues.zh: 想想看，把三万人相当均匀地分散在地球表面。你可能过完一辈子，都遇不到另一个人。

cues.en: The degree of ignorance and arrogance in her reply is staggering.
cues.zh: 她回复中的无知和傲慢程度令人震惊。

cues.en: First, the number is 42,000,
cues.zh: 首先，数量是4.2万颗，

cues.en: not 30. That's how many satellites you wanna put up.
cues.zh: 不是30颗。这就是你想发射的卫星数量。

cues.en: Second, humans don't move at 25,000
cues.zh: 其次，人类不会以每小时2.5万

cues.en: kilometers per hour.
cues.zh: 公里的速度移动。

cues.en: Third, if they ever did run into each other at that speed, they would completely liquefy each other.
cues.zh: 第三，如果它们真的以那种速度相撞，会彻底把彼此撞成液态。

cues.en: And finally, these satellites cross each other's paths constantly
cues.zh: 最后，这些卫星经常交叉彼此的路径

cues.en: just as they're doing in this video. On this path, these two trains of Starlinks zip through each other without incident,
cues.zh: 就像它们在这段视频里所做的那样。在这条路径上，这两列星链卫星呼啸着交错而过，相安无事，

cues.en: but it will only take one time where a nonresponsive satellite knocks another one out of orbit, and that will accelerate the Kessler syndrome prediction.
cues.zh: 但只需一次，一颗无响应的卫星把另一颗撞出轨道，就会加速凯斯勒综合征的预测成真。

cues.en: We say accelerate rather than initiate because the Kessler syndrome has already begun.
cues.zh: 我们说“加速”而不是“启动”，因为凯斯勒效应已经开始了。

cues.en: NASA and CSA reported finding a five millimeter hole blasted through the ISS's Canadarm tube. The Canadarm booms are made of graphite epoxy and are protected by bulletproof Kevlar sleeves. So whatever projectile this was went straight through two layers of each material.
cues.zh: NASA 和 CSA 报告称，ISS 的 Canadarm 管上被击穿了一个直径五毫米的孔。Canadarm 的机械臂由石墨环氧材料制成，外面包着防弹凯夫拉套管。因此，无论是什么东西撞上去，都直接穿透了这两种材料的两层。

cues.en: That is just the latest object collision on the ISS. It certainly will not be the last one.
cues.zh: 这只是 ISS 最近发生的一次物体碰撞，当然不会是最后一次。

cues.en: The point being made here is there are already collisions happening in space.
cues.zh: 这里的核心观点是，太空中其实已经在发生碰撞了。

cues.en: Every time there is a collision in orbit, additional pieces are flying into space as a result. If every collision results in the original piece knocking loose one additional piece, that would double the number of projectiles.
cues.zh: 轨道上每次发生碰撞，都会产生更多碎片飞入太空。如果每次碰撞都导致原本的碎片撞落出另一块新碎片，抛射物的数量就会直接翻倍。

cues.en: If it knocks two loose, now you've tripled the number. So this becomes an exponential function, not unlike those shampoo commercials where you tell two friends and they tell two friends and so on. And so on. And so on.
cues.zh: 要是撞落两块，数量就会变成三倍。这就变成了一个指数级增长，就像洗发水广告里说的那样，你告诉两个朋友，他们再各自告诉两个朋友，依此类推。以此类推。一直传下去。

cues.en: In the early days where we are now, that function is in the early stages. Since we are adding to the population of orbital debris at a greater rate than we are subtracting from it, we are increasing the rate at which this is happening.
cues.zh: 我们现在所处的早期阶段，这项功能还处于初期。我们增加轨道碎片的速度快于减少的速度，因此这种情况发生的频率在加快。

cues.en: This is why some space agencies like JAXA are looking for solutions to clear Earth's orbit from the tens of thousands of pieces of orbital debris they can track and the millions of smaller pieces that are too small to be tracked, but still carry the potential energy of a cannonball.
cues.zh: 这就是为什么像 JAXA 这样的航天机构正在寻找解决方案，以清除地球轨道上可追踪的数万块碎片，以及数百万太小而无法追踪但仍具有炮弹般潜在能量的碎片。

cues.en: Once the Kessler syndrome starts picking up speed in the middle of the scenario, these collisions will become more and more frequent, creating more and more shrapnel.
cues.zh: 当凯斯勒综合征在推演中期开始加速时，这些碰撞会越来越频繁，产生越来越多的碎片。

cues.en: And at the end of it, we could well be left with a field of debris surrounding the planet that prevents any launches to any orbital elevation.
cues.zh: 到最后，地球周围很可能会变成一片碎片场，阻止任何飞行器进入任何轨道高度。

cues.en: Since the declared intentions of Musk are to launch humankind to the moon and to Mars, where he intends to ascend to the emperor's throne, he should absolutely be completely protective of those orbits by keeping them as clear as possible,
cues.zh: 既然马斯克声称要把人类送上月球和火星，还打算在那里登基称帝，他就应该尽全力保护这些轨道，尽可能保持轨道畅通，

cues.en: especially in light of the thin skinned starships that he's planning to use to fulfill his Christopher Columbus fantasies.
cues.zh: 尤其考虑到他计划使用的飞船外壳很薄，来实现他那哥伦布式的幻想。

cues.en: This is what happens when a 14 gram piece of plastic moving at orbital velocity collides with a solid block of aluminum.
cues.zh: 这就是一块 14 克的塑料以轨道速度撞击实心铝块时的效果。

cues.en: And this is the result from the same test using a one centimeter sphere of aluminum instead of plastic.
cues.zh: 而这是把塑料换成一厘米大的铝球后，同一测试得到的结果。

cues.en: For illustrative purposes, let's compare these impacts with a 50 caliber round hitting a stainless steel plate. Velocity of this round is 3,000 feet or about 1,000 meters per second, and the projectile weighs about 50 grams. These rounds go straight through a stainless steel plate that's three quarters of an inch thick, around two centimeters or 20 millimeters. Straight through. And the thickness of the stainless steel skin on Starship
cues.zh: 为了更直观，我们把这些撞击与一颗点 50 口径子弹击中不锈钢板的情况对比一下。该弹丸的速度为每秒 3,000 英尺，约合 1,000 米，重约 50 克。这种子弹能直接穿透四分之三英寸（约 2 厘米或 20 毫米）厚的不锈钢板。直接打穿。而 Starship 的不锈钢外壳厚度

cues.en: is currently at four millimeters with plans to go as low as two millimeters.
cues.zh: 目前只有 4 毫米，甚至还计划进一步降到 2 毫米。

cues.en: Every single object in orbit will breach that skin like paper since everything in orbit moves about 10 times faster than that bullet.
cues.zh: 轨道上的每个物体都会像纸一样被击穿，因为轨道上所有物体的运动速度大约是那颗子弹的10倍。

cues.zh: 现在来看看这项卫星服务的全球市场可能有多大。在最近的一次采访中，Gwen Shotwell表示，Starlink希望利用其卫星网络打入她所说的万亿美元市场。

cues.zh: 所以肖特韦尔女士，SpaceX的总裁，马斯克的得力助手兼私人传声筒，认为他们能以某种方式平均榨取127美元

cues.zh: 每五个家庭每年。

cues.zh: 我们不禁要怀疑她是不是很少出远门。

cues.zh: 看来过惯了高管奢华生活、身家大概3亿美元的 Shotwell 女士，

cues.zh: 根本不知道地球上的绝大多数人，根本掏不出这种闲钱来享受上网这种“奢侈品”。

cues.zh: 用户可以点击世界上任意一个国家，查看该国目前的年平均收入。

cues.zh: 深红色国家每年不到1000美元

cues.zh: 按每个劳动者计算。全球人口最多的两个国家中国和印度都处于红色区域。墨西哥也是如此，世界数据显示其人均年收入为9480美元

cues.en: per person.
cues.zh: 每人。

cues.en: If miss Shotwell thinks she will be selling $500 signal boxes and $100 per month subscriptions to these large populations of people, she needs to give that blonde wig a shake.
cues.zh: 如果 Shotwell 以为自己能向这些庞大的人群出售 500 美元的信号盒，再收取每月 100 美元的订阅费，那她可得清醒清醒了。

cues.zh: 这样剩下加拿大和美国，

cues.zh: 欧洲的大部分国家（但不是全部）、澳大利亚、

cues.zh: 新西兰、日本，以及中东和南美的少数几个国家。

cues.en: And guess what? Every single one of those countries is already serviced with global broadband Internet through the existing oceanic cable system,
cues.zh: 你猜怎么着？这些国家里的每一个，其实都已经通过现有的海底光缆系统接入了全球宽带互联网，

cues.en: into which Starship will have to tap anyway.
cues.zh: 而 Starship 无论如何也必须接入这个系统。

cues.en: That's something else that people seem to have overlooked.
cues.zh: 这也是人们似乎忽视了的另一件事。

cues.en: The Starlink constellation will never outperform the ground based nexus because it still has to tie in to that same system. It will never be faster or have a better ping rating than the core system itself.
cues.zh: Starlink 星座的性能永远无法超越地面网络核心节点，因为它仍然必须接入同一个系统。它的速度绝不可能比核心系统本身更快，延迟表现也不可能更好。

cues.en: People will always be better off with a cable connection. It's cheaper, it's faster,
cues.zh: 用有线连接，人们总是过得更好。它更便宜、更快，

cues.en: and it's more reliable.
cues.zh: 也更可靠。

cues.en: Which is probably why the worldwide satellite Internet market, while expected to be a growth industry,
cues.zh: 这大概就是为什么全球卫星互联网市场，虽然预计会成为增长型行业，

cues.en: is valued at only $3,424,000,000
in May 2021 and is forecasted to roughly double by 2026
cues.zh: 而预计到2026年大致会翻一番，

cues.en: So if miss Shotwell captured the entire global satellite industry, put everyone else out of business, and stood alone as the sole provider of satellite Internet in the world, she would manage to make about one half of 1% the amount of money she says Starlink is poised to create for her boss. In other words, she's completely speaking out of her ass.
cues.zh: 所以，如果Shotwell女士拿下了整个全球卫星产业，把其他所有人都挤出局，独自成为全世界卫星互联网的唯一供应商，她能赚到的钱，大约也只有她说Starlink将为她老板创造的钱的0.5%。换句话说，她完全是在胡说八道。

cues.en: Kind of like when she told that TED talk in 2018.
cues.zh: 有点像她在 2018 年做那场 TED 演讲时说的。

cues.en: Oh, no. It's definitely gonna happen. This is definitely gonna happen.
cues.zh: 哦，不，这肯定会发生。这事肯定会发生。

cues.en: How?
cues.zh: 怎么会？

cues.en: Taking a hard look at the numbers can determine pretty quickly that they just do not add up. You'd have to be completely oblivious to give Musk any money for this at all. You'd have to be almost as clueless as the federal government.
cues.zh: 仔细看看这些数字，很快就能发现根本对不上。要是还给马斯克投钱，那你简直就是完全不长脑子，跟联邦政府一样糊涂。

cues.en: Yep. In December 2020, the FCC announced that SpaceX was one of the satellite Internet providers chosen to receive almost a billion dollars in payers money to set up their constellation to service 642,925
cues.zh: 没错。2020 年 12 月，FCC 宣布 SpaceX 是获选的卫星互联网服务商之一，将获得近 10 亿美元的纳税人资金，用来部署卫星星座，为美国境内的 642,925

cues.en: locations across The US.
cues.zh: 个地点提供服务。

cues.en: This is a Musk project. Of course, there's a government subsidy that he can bleed dry.
cues.zh: 这是 Musk 的项目，自然少不了能让他狠狠薅一把的政府补贴。

cues.en: This is how much money the FCC earmarked for Starlink,
cues.zh: 这是 FCC 给 Starlink 划拨的资金：

cues.en: This is how many locations Musk needs the service, 642,925.
cues.zh: 这是 Musk 需要提供服务的地点数量：642,925 处。

cues.en: So this is how much the FCC is prepared to pay per location for Musk to do what he promised,
cues.zh: 算下来，为了让 Musk 兑现承诺，FCC 准备为每个地点支付这么多钱：

cues.en: per location.
cues.zh: 按每处地点算。

cues.en: But that won't even cover the equipment cost of the kit that Starlink has to send out to each of those addresses.
cues.zh: 但这笔钱甚至不够覆盖 Starlink 寄往各地的硬件设备成本。

cues.en: This FCC money is not guaranteed, and it won't come in a lump sum. It's based on performance, and it will be split over the next ten years payable in monthly installments.
cues.zh: 这笔FCC资金并无保障，也不会一次性到账。它取决于实际表现，并将在未来十年内按月分期支付。

cues.en: In order to receive any of the money, Starlink has to prove the system's ability to service those customers maintaining a latency rate under one hundred milliseconds while providing speeds of 100 megabits per second downstream and 20 megabits per second upstream.
cues.zh: 要拿到任何资金，Starlink必须证明系统有能力服务这些用户，保持延迟低于100毫秒，同时提供下行100兆比特每秒、上行20兆比特每秒的速度。

cues.en: Something odd about this process is that in June 2020, the FCC released a report throwing doubt on Starlink's ability to make good on their claims.
cues.zh: 这个过程中有件奇怪的事：2020年6月，FCC发布了一份报告，对 Starlink 能否兑现承诺表示怀疑。

cues.en: They were not convinced that Starlink would be able to provide the speeds and latency required to qualify for what they called the RDOF
cues.zh: 他们不确定 Starlink 能否达到规定的速度和延迟要求，从而符合他们所称的 RDOF

cues.en: or rural digital opportunity fund.
cues.zh: 也就是农村数字机会基金。

cues.en: It's a concern that was seconded by Ookla in May 2021.
cues.zh: Ookla 在 2021 年 5 月也提出了同样的担忧。

cues.en: As one of the top apps for measuring such metrics, Ookla believes that the system might eventually qualify for the upload speeds,
cues.zh: 作为测量这类指标的顶尖应用之一，Ookla 认为这个系统最终或许能达到上传速度要求，

cues.en: but is already falling well short on the download speeds.
cues.zh: 但目前的下载速度已经远远不达标。

cues.en: Meaning that Starlink won't qualify for the RDOF subsidy because they will not hit the benchmarks.
cues.zh: 这意味着 Starlink 将拿不到 RDOF 补贴，因为他们达不到那些指标。

cues.en: So it's a mystery why in December 2020, the FCC suddenly announced SpaceX had won the low latency auction aspect of their subsidy program, and they were tentatively awarding SpaceX almost $1,000,000,000 spread over ten years in monthly payments. cues.zh: 所以这就成了一个谜：为什么在 2020 年 12 月，FCC 突然宣布 SpaceX 赢得了该补贴项目的低延迟竞标，并初步决定在十年内按月向 SpaceX 拨付近 10 亿美元。显然，他们突然看到了某些东西，改变了想法，并让他们觉得这终究是一笔划算的投资。

cues.zh: 天哪，他们错得离谱。

cues.zh: 在FCC表达疑虑一年后，也就是他们改变主意并宣布SpaceX为拍卖中标者六个月后，马斯克现在向全世界宣称，Starlink已经濒临破产，他还需要另外300亿美元

cues.zh: 而且他需要尽快拿到这笔钱，以避免破产。

cues.zh: 那他到底打算怎么做到呢？

cues.en: We've already gone through the money losing machine that Starlink is likely to be. And when a company needs to raise a bunch of money quickly to stop the bleeding of red ink, there are three little letters that they tend to turn to.
cues.zh: 我们已经聊过 Starlink 很可能会是个烧钱机器。公司要是急着筹一大笔钱来止住亏损，往往会想到三个字母。

cues.en: And wouldn't you know it, Musk is already teasing the idea of spinning Starlink off from SpaceX with, you got it, an IPO.
cues.zh: 你猜怎么着？马斯克已经在放风，称要把 Starlink 从 SpaceX 分拆出来，没错，就是通过 IPO。

cues.en: On June 24, as we were finalizing the script for this video, this article came out, and to absolutely nobody's surprise, Musk is already teasing an initial public offering.
cues.zh: 6 月 24 日，我们正在敲定这期视频的稿子时，这篇文章发布了。毫不意外，马斯克已经在放风，称要进行首次公开募股。

cues.zh: 他表示，这将在 Starlink 的收入变得更加可预测时发生。

cues.en: An initial public offering is when a company decides to sell shares to the public and allow them to be exchanged on the open market. This is often done when companies believe they are ready for the scrutiny and reporting practices that are required, but it's also done to try to keep companies afloat with an infusion of shareholder money on the open market.
cues.zh: 首次公开募股是指公司决定向公众出售股份，并允许这些股份在公开市场交易。公司通常在认为自己做好了应对所需严格审查和财报披露的准备时这样做，但有时也是为了通过公开市场上股东的资金注入，来维持公司的运转。

cues.en: And the best way, as Musk knows, to drive up the price of that IPO is with hype.
cues.zh: 而抬高那场IPO价格的最佳方式，正如马斯克所知，就是炒作。

cues.en: Now here is the short list of reasons why you will want to stay the hell away from the Starlink IPO.
cues.zh: 下面简短列出你为何要极力远离Starlink IPO的几个原因。

cues.en: First off, as we've already outlined, this system is unremarkable and will lose money hand over fist.
cues.zh: 首先，正如我们已概述的，这套系统平平无奇，将大把亏钱。

cues.en: Second, the declared intention of Musk is to use Starlink revenues to finance future SpaceX operations.
cues.zh: 第二，马斯克公开的意图是用Starlink的收入为未来的SpaceX运营提供资金。

cues.en: They will be spinning off Starlink,
cues.zh: 他们将分拆Starlink，

cues.en: offering an IPO on Starlink, not SpaceX.
cues.zh: 对Starlink而非SpaceX进行IPO。

cues.en: Yet the revenue stream of Starlink is meant to benefit another privately held Musk company of which the shareholders will have no stake.
cues.zh: 然而，Starlink 的收入本应让另一家由 Musk 私人持有的公司受益，而股东在这家公司里没有任何权益。

cues.en: In order to spin off an IPO for Starlink, it will have to become a separate entity from SpaceX.
cues.zh: 要让 Starlink 通过分拆进行 IPO，它就必须从 SpaceX 中独立出来。

cues.en: But then it's going to send all the revenue that it makes to this other company?
cues.zh: 可它之后要把赚到的所有收入都交给这另一家公司吗？

cues.en: These two statements made by Musk are in direct opposition to each other. If the idea of Starlink is to create an unending source of money for Musk to use to further his off world enterprises,
cues.zh: Musk 的这两种说法直接相互矛盾。如果 Starlink 的目的是为 Musk 创造源源不断的资金，让他继续拓展地外事业，

cues.en: then he will need to keep as much of that revenue to himself as possible.
cues.zh: 那他就得尽可能把这些收入留给自己。

cues.en: If the company goes public, then he would have to split that wealth in return for a lump sum earned at the release of the IPO.
cues.zh: 如果公司上市，他就得把这笔财富分出去，换取 IPO 发行时获得的一笔巨款。

cues.en: The only way that SpaceX would be able to make money from those shares is either by declaring dividends that are payable to all shareholders in that share class or by speculating in the stock.
cues.zh: SpaceX 要想从这些股份中获利，要么向该股同类股东派发股息，要么进行股票投机。

cues.en: If Musk intends to keep all of those dividends to himself,
cues.zh: 如果 Musk 打算把这些分红全留给自己，

cues.en: then he and SpaceX would buy preferred shares
cues.zh: 那他和 SpaceX 就会买入优先股，

cues.en: and release only common shares to the general public. Here's the thing. Musk doesn't pay dividends ever.
cues.zh: 只向公众公开发行普通股。但问题在于，Musk 从来不分红。

cues.en: Tesla is supposed to be one of the biggest companies in the world by market cap, but shareholders have never received one thin dime in dividends.
cues.zh: 按市值算，特斯拉本应是全球最大的公司之一，但股东们从未拿到过一分钱股息。

cues.en: Musk won't be able to pay out just one group of people unless he does a different series of shares where preferred shares will get paid out dividends,
cues.zh: 马斯克没法只给某一群人分红，除非他搞出不同类别的股票，让优先股能拿到股息，

cues.en: while common shares will get paid nothing.
cues.zh: 而普通股一分钱都拿不到。

cues.en: And again, we'll use Tesla as an example here. The Tesla shareholder agreement states quite clearly
cues.zh: 同样，我们这里还是拿特斯拉举例。特斯拉的股东协议写得非常清楚：

cues.en: that Tesla has never and will not be paying out dividends on their shares in the foreseeable future.
cues.zh: 特斯拉从未、也不会在可预见的未来对股票派发股息。

cues.en: This also takes us back full circle to SolarCity.
cues.zh: 这也让我们兜了一圈，回到了SolarCity。

cues.en: SolarCity went public in December 2012 with an IPO price of $8,
cues.zh: SolarCity于2012年12月上市，IPO发行价为8美元，
募集了9200万美元，

cues.en: for the company to put towards purchasing the equipment that they were then leasing to their customers.
cues.zh: 供公司购买设备，再将这些设备租给客户。

cues.en: The hype surrounding this supposedly groundbreaking revolutionary new company drove the share price well over $80 from the $8 IPO.
cues.zh: 这家自称带来突破性革命的新公司的热度，把股价从8美元的IPO发行价推高到了80多美元。

cues.en: But from there, the stock lost over 75%
cues.zh: 但此后，股价下跌了超过75%，

cues.en: of its share price to close at $20.36
cues.zh: 收于20.36美元。

cues.en: when Tesla bailed Musk and his cousins out on 11/01/2016
cues.zh: 2016年11月1日，Tesla出手解救了Musk和他的表亲们，

cues.en: about four years later.
cues.zh: 那时距离上市大约四年。

cues.en: Turned out those shares were still way overpriced as the company was insolvent at the time of acquisition.
cues.zh: 事实证明，这些股票的估值依然高得离谱，因为收购时该公司已经资不抵债了。

cues.en: On top of the $2,800,000,000
cues.zh: 除了28亿美元的

cues.en: purchase price, Tesla also had to take on $3,000,000,000
cues.zh: 收购价格之外，Tesla 还不得不承担30亿美元

cues.en: in solar city debt.
cues.zh: SolarCity 的债务。

cues.en: This company that had been fond over by the press for years promising the most efficient solar panels in the world was actually using cheap Chinese components in their installation and they were losing money on every contract.
cues.zh: 这家多年来被媒体极力吹捧、承诺制造世界上最高效太阳能电池板的公司，实际上安装时用的都是廉价的中国零部件，而且他们每签一单都在亏钱。

cues.en: This is what will happen with Starlink as well. It is the same model and it will have the same result. Another hyped up Musk fantasy.
cues.zh: Starlink也会是这样。同样的模式，同样的结果。又一个被吹上天的马斯克式幻想。

cues.en: You'd think that people would learn.
cues.zh: 你可能会以为人们会吸取教训。

cues.en: And one more thing about Musk and the prospect of an IPO for Starlink.
cues.zh: 还有一点关于马斯克和Starlink上市前景的事。

cues.en: Musk hates the SEC,
cues.zh: 马斯克恨SEC，

cues.en: hates them, ridicules them, taunts them. He's been fined heavily by them for his past antics.
cues.zh: 恨他们，嘲讽他们，奚落他们。他过去那些荒唐行为已经被他们罚了重款。

cues.en: But he will have to deal with them on a whole new level if this IPO were to move forward.
cues.zh: 但如果这次IPO真的推进，他将不得不在一个全新的层面上与他们打交道。

cues.en: He would have to kiss their ass and keep his mouth shut,
cues.zh: 他就得对他们卑躬屈膝，还得闭上嘴，

cues.en: which as we all know are not his strong suits.
cues.zh: 可我们都知道，这两点都不是他的强项。

cues.en: All things considered,
cues.zh: 综合来看，

cues.en: if Starlink splinters from SpaceX and Musk is forced to go that route, it's pretty much going to be a last ditch effort to bail him out again.
cues.zh: 如果 Starlink 脱离 SpaceX，而 Musk 被迫走这条路，那基本上就是他再次脱身的最后一搏。

cues.en: And this time, investors would serve themselves well to stay clear of it as it goes down.
cues.zh: 这一次，投资者最好远离它，免得跟着它一起沉下去。

cues.en: Now if you're thinking this assessment is biased in any way, ask yourself this.
cues.zh: 如果你觉得这番判断有失偏颇，不妨问问自己：

cues.en: Can you name a single publicly traded company that siphons all of its profits and revenues back to the original private enterprise?
cues.zh: 你能说出哪怕一家上市公司，会把所有利润和营收都倒流回最初的私企吗？

cues.en: If you can, leave that information in the comments.
cues.zh: 要是能想到，欢迎在评论区告诉我。

cues.en: With regards to the Starlink system itself, there are additional concerns. We've already mentioned that these sealed units are not user serviceable or in fact serviceable at all even by professionals.
cues.zh: 至于 Starlink 系统本身，还有其他令人担忧的地方。我们之前提到过，这些密封设备用户根本无法自行维修，事实上就算是专业人员也修不了。

cues.en: Considering that according to the terms and conditions of the Starlink agreement, these dishes are being sold to you completely as is, that should be a real red flag, and Caveat Emptors should be waving you off from that purchase.
cues.zh: 考虑到根据 Starlink 协议的条款和条件，这些天线设备完全是以“现状”出售的，这绝对是个巨大的危险信号，“买者自负”的警钟早该劝退你下单了。

cues.en: Here are some of the other reasons why choosing Starlink probably won't be a good fit for North Americans.
cues.zh: 以下是 Starlink 可能不适合北美人的一些其他原因。

cues.en: One of the first things you need to realize is that the service is not suitable for people living in high density areas. The satellites do not have the bandwidth required to handle that type of traffic, and they will work best only for people who are well removed from the cities.
cues.zh: 你首先需要意识到的一点是，这项服务不适合居住在高密度地区的人。卫星没有处理那种流量所需的带宽，它们只在远离城市的人那里效果最好。

cues.en: Reports are common across social media now that single trees can cause you to lose your Internet connection with Starlink, which is fair enough. Trees block signals, but not everyone is going to want to clear cut their property around the house before they can Netflix and chill.
cues.zh: 现在社交媒体上经常有报告说，单棵树就能让你失去 Starlink 的互联网连接，这很合理。树木会阻挡信号，但不是每个人都愿意为了看 Netflix 放松一下而把房子周围的树全砍光。

cues.en: And for that matter, the tree that's blocking your signal might not even be on your property.
cues.zh: 况且，挡住你信号的那棵树甚至可能不在你的地界上。

cues.en: Additional issues include reports that are now out indicating the system is unable to perform in conditions lower than minus 30 degrees Celsius and above 40 degrees Celsius. In Fahrenheit, that's minus 22 to one zero four as the internal temperature of the dish.
cues.zh: 其他问题还包括近期有报告指出，系统在低于零下30摄氏度或高于40摄氏度的环境下无法工作。换算成华氏度，就是零下22度到104度，这是设备内部的温度范围。

cues.en: Now the lower end of that scale will not affect most of the lower 48,
cues.zh: 这个温度范围的低端不会影响美国本土48州的大多数地区，

cues.en: but Alaska and many parts of Canada do get well below minus 30 degrees Celsius during an average winter. But the high end of that definitely creates a problem for the Continental US.
cues.zh: 但阿拉斯加和加拿大许多地区在普通冬季都会远低于零下30摄氏度。高端温度则确实会给美国本土带来问题。

cues.en: Something a beta tester in Arizona found out the hard way when his dish overheated and it had to be hosed down by the owner, who decided build a canopy for the device to give it shade and save on his water bill. Temperatures across the Southern US often go north of 40 degrees Celsius. Southern California,
cues.zh: 亚利桑那州的一位公测用户就吃过这种苦头：当时他的天线过热，不得不拿水管浇水降温，最后他决定给设备搭个遮阳棚，好给它遮阳并省点水费；美国南部的气温经常会飙升到40摄氏度以上，南加州、

cues.en: Arizona, New Mexico, Texas, they have no problem hitting that mark in a normal year. So on the hottest days of the year, you can expect to lose your Starlink connection.
cues.zh: 亚利桑那州、新墨西哥州、德克萨斯州，在正常年份达到这个温度完全不在话下，所以在一年中最热的那些天里，你的 Starlink 连接很可能会断掉。

cues.en: And in areas prone to electrical storms, it would appear that customers who don't use professional third party installers might be lighting themselves up for another shock as dishes have already been hit and destroyed by lightning.
cues.zh: 在容易发生雷暴的地区，看来不使用专业第三方安装商的客户，可能会让自己再次遭受电击，因为天线已经被闪电击中并损坏了。

cues.en: We'll wrap up this segment with a question. When you have to buy another dish from Starlink because the one that you had got buggered up, is the company going to charge you the same $500 for the replacement system, or are they going to charge you their full cost of it so that they don't lose another $1,500
cues.zh: 我们用一个问题来结束本节。当你因为原来的天线被弄坏了而不得不从Starlink再买一个天线时，公司会向你收取同样的500美元更换系统费用，还是会向你收取他们的全额成本，以免在你身上再损失1500美元？

cues.en: on you? Maybe somebody could ask Musk that question on Twitter to see what kind of response you get, and then you can share it here so we can all get a good laugh.
cues.zh: on you? 也许有人可以在Twitter上向Musk问这个问题，看看你会得到什么样的回应，然后你可以在这里分享，让我们都能好好笑一场。

cues.en: If all the other aspects of this system weren't bad enough,
cues.zh: 如果这个系统的其他方面还不够糟糕，

cues.en: Starlink satellites are posing an additional threat to the entire planet through their destruction of land based astronomy.
cues.zh: Starlink 卫星还在通过破坏地面天文学，对整个地球构成额外威胁。

cues.en: Over the past year, there's been a steady stream of pictures show up line from amateur astronomers demonstrating how the Starlink satellites in orbit are already making it difficult to do time lapse photography that they require for hobbyist photos or sky watching.
cues.zh: 过去一年里，业余天文学家不断晒出照片，显示轨道上的 Starlink 卫星已经让延时摄影变得困难，而这正是他们拍摄业余作品或观星所需要的。

cues.en: Perfect example here would when people last year were trying to capture images of that once in a lifetime NEOWISE comet. But it's not just the amateurs who are having difficulty with this. The professional land based observatories are having the same problems.
cues.zh: 一个绝佳的例子就是去年人们争相拍摄那颗千载难逢的 NEOWISE 彗星。但遇到这种麻烦的可不仅是业余天文爱好者，专业的地面天文台也面临着同样的困扰。

cues.en: Trains of Starlink satellites sweeping through a time lapse capture completely destroy the image. But those images are not just to put up on somebody's Facebook or Instagram pages. These images are studied and poured over to detect near Earth objects.
cues.zh: 成列的 Starlink 卫星划过延时拍摄的画面，会彻底毁掉整张照片。而这些图像可不只是用来发在 Facebook 或 Instagram 上的，科学家们需要仔细研究并审视它们，以此来探测近地天体。

cues.en: And to make things even more difficult, the best time to detect these objects is during the twilight hours,
cues.zh: 更麻烦的是，探测这些天体的最佳时段是暮光时分，

cues.en: which happens to be when the Starlink satellites are the most visible in the sky. And, of course, the Starlink constellation will only become more and more of a hindrance as its population in orbit increases.
cues.zh: 而这恰好也是 Starlink 卫星在天空中最显眼的时候。当然，随着 Starlink 星座在轨数量不断增加，它只会越来越成为障碍。

cues.en: But not to worry because Elon Musk has already told his followers that Starlink won't affect ground based astronomy at all.
cues.zh: 但不用担心，因为 Elon Musk 已经告诉他的粉丝，Starlink 根本不会影响地面天文观测。

cues.en: Way to ignore the indisputable
cues.zh: 想无视无可辩驳的

cues.en: evidence, you jackass.
cues.zh: 证据，你这个混蛋。

cues.en: So after all the analysis, all the digging, article reading, video watching, and calculating,
cues.zh: 经过一番分析、深挖、阅读文章、观看视频和计算，

cues.en: here are the conclusions that anyone paying attention should come to regarding Starlink.
cues.zh: 下面是所有认真关注的人都应该得出的关于 Starlink 的结论。

cues.en: First, the Starlink constellation adds no new product to the marketplace.
cues.zh: 第一，Starlink 星座没有为市场带来任何新产品。

cues.en: Second, according to one of the top latency measuring apps, Starlink is unlikely to provide a significant speed advantage to the existing products.
cues.zh: 第二，根据一款顶尖的延迟测量应用，Starlink 不太可能比现有产品快多少。

cues.en: Third, the market for this product is pretty much restricted to the remote locations of North America, Europe, and Australia,
cues.zh: 第三，这款产品的市场基本仅限于北美、欧洲和澳大利亚的偏远地区，

cues.en: all of whom are already covered by other providers.
cues.zh: 而这些地方早就被其他服务商覆盖了。

cues.en: The rest of the world needs running water more than it needs satellite internet.
cues.zh: 对于世界其他地区来说，自来水可比卫星互联网重要得多。

cues.en: Fourth, the number of satellites being proposed by Musk significantly accelerates the incident rate required to realize a full Kessler syndrome annihilation of objects in orbit, which at 550 kilometers LEO could create a shroud of shrapnel around the Earth that prevents any other spacecraft from being launched.
cues.zh: 第四，Musk 提议发射的卫星数量，大幅加快了触发完全凯斯勒综合征所需的事故发生率；而在 550 公里的近地轨道上，这可能会在地球周围形成一层弹片罩，彻底阻断其他航天器的发射。

cues.en: Fifth,
cues.zh: 第五，

cues.en: this is not a trillion dollar industry that they're trying to tap into. In fact, it's not even projected to be a $10,000,000,000
cues.zh: 这并不是他们试图开拓的万亿美元产业。事实上，未来五年全球范围内，这个产业的规模预计甚至都达不到100亿美元

cues.en: industry globally in the next five years.
Sixth, the constellation as is already jeopardizes ground based astronomers ability to detect asteroids threatening to collide with Earth and make other scientific discoveries.
cues.zh: 第六，这个卫星星座本身已经危及地基天文学家探测可能撞向地球的小行星的能力，以及他们做出其他科学发现的能力。

cues.en: And seventh,
cues.zh: 第七，

cues.en: Musk promising an IPO issuance on a spun off Starlink will pretty much signal to the world that this model is yet another Musk failure requiring requiring bailout.
cues.zh: 马斯克承诺将分拆出来的Starlink进行IPO发行，这几乎等于向全世界发出信号：这个模式不过是马斯克的又一次失败，需要救助。

cues.en: Just wait until Rocket Jesus tells you this is a no brainer, and that's when everyone will know for sure.
cues.zh: 等 Rocket Jesus 告诉你这根本不用动脑子时，大家就都能确定了。
